newsitem.title: USA: IDT enters deal with six states, cuts jobs.
newsitem.headline: IDT enters deal with six states, cuts jobs.

text.p: IDT Corp on Wednesday said it entered a settlement with Attorneys General in six states over its Internet access service.
IDT also said it is shifting its focus to its telecommunications division and away from its dial-up Internet access operation, resulting in the layoffs of 120 sales and marketing employees.
IDT, which has 150,000 Internet access customers, it is not leaving the business and will continue advertising, despite the job cuts, a company spokeswoman said.

In the settlement with attorneys general Iowa, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, Tennessee and Texas, IDT said it will have to reimburse customers the costs for certain ITD services and specific calls into IDT Internet's technical support.
IDT was not immediately available to determine the extent of the costs to be reimbursed.

The company said it also offered severance packages for dismissed employees. Included in the package is any stock options previously guaranteed to IDT employees, either prior to the initial public offering, or as incentive arrangements, the company said.

The total streamlining of staff and operations is expected to cut about 20 percent per month from IDT's payroll cost, IDT said. The job cuts are expected to make the company more profitable within the next few months and are not expected to affect projected revenue growth, IDT said.
